claims.statement: CLI computer use is explicitly public preview and subject to change; availability is not a stable production guarantee.

The published body describes reading accessible/visual application content and performing clicks, text edits, keys, scrolling, dragging and cross-application navigation; no action is executed by review.
The published scope is local macOS and Windows sessions, useful for GUI-only workflows; this does not establish remote unattended computer control.
The status command reports plugin, MCP server and associated skills separately; a command description is not actual status evidence.
The enable command persists a preference and enables the bundled plugin; managed organizational disabling cannot be overridden by that local preference.
macOS operation requires Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions; source review neither grants nor verifies them.
The guidance recommends specifying outcome, applications and constraints; the read-only example explicitly avoids value changes and form submission.
Active CLI permission mode determines whether application control requests approval; a permission-mode check is described, not performed.
Allow is session-scoped, Always allow saves future-session approval, and declining/canceling remains possible when approval is required.
Saved application approval is shared with the Copilot app on the same computer; approval scope extends beyond the current CLI session.
The source recommends checking that the requested application/action matches intent; configured deny rules take precedence over saved approval.
Pressing Escape twice is the documented interruption path; successful stopping or recovery is not verified here.
The disable command is followed by a status check to confirm plugin and MCP server disabled; a preference write alone is not verified shutdown.
Unavailable status requires checking account feature availability, local-session scope and supported operating system.
Enabled-but-failing operation requires separately checking bundled plugin enablement and MCP connectivity.
The macOS troubleshooting requirement reiterates both Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions; absence must not be treated as PASS.
